names: The provisioned project is the template plus the addon, with no laboratory directory
The project enables the addon's plugin and names its application Resource
The scene injects the addon's facade and no script of the project names a path to the laboratory SDK or the global class
The scene's root is the GameServices node, with the Application, the World and a HUD surface under it
The HUD is public TSX: it imports only react, react-native, @godot-fabric/runtime and its own types
The provisioned guide links the research note at the provisioned revision
Editor build preserves the project lockfile
The consumer executes its bundle once, for ten cycles
The report holds one measurement for each of the ten cycles
Nodes (21), orphans (0), subscriptions (1), snapshot_changed connections (2) and HUD connections (1) are the first cycle's after every cycle
Every cycle ends with the 14 bindings, nothing pending and exactly one World
The epoch rises by exactly the three new games of each cycle, strictly, and the HUD and Godot agree on it
Every cycle went to the menu with no World and no HUD connection, freed the Worlds it dropped, and every call was accepted
The headed run also ran the ten cycles
The bundle has no laboratory, examples or SDK-checkout source, and no project dependency
The bundle is built from the project's own TSX: the HUD and the types of the services
The provisioned build works with network denied and no global Node, and gives the same bundle
Building and running preserve the project lockfile

droppedSabotage.name: world-leak
droppedSabotage.was: the World drops its subscription without calling stop() when it leaves the tree
droppedSabotage.why: That leak cannot happen: Godot 4.7.2 drops a connection whose target is a freed Node by itself, lambdas made inside a Node included. Only a lambda made by a RefCounted outlives its object, and the first design of the World wrapped its handler in such an object (a RefCounted `Subscription`) for no purpose but to make the sabotage possible. The World now connects a plain method and disconnects it explicitly in _exit_tree, and the per-cycle count of the connections of snapshot_changed stays as a guard.

experiment.reading: the RefCounted method's connection went with its object when its last reference did, both Node connections went with the nodes, and only the lambda made by the RefCounted stayed; a removed node that is not freed is an orphan and is not in get_node_count()

editedAfterTheRuns.note: After the commands ran, these four files only gained links to this record (and, in docs/evidence/README.md, its index entry). consumers/civ-lite/README.md is read by the check only to rewrite its ../../ links, and the SHA-256 above is the one it had when it ran.

limits: The HUD is the minimal service HUD (the turn, the context, the actions with their reasons, Menu and New game), not the playable one: that is V05-05 and V05-08. The scenery draws the map and takes no input.

The presses are synthetic: a mouse down and up pushed through the viewport on the centre of each Pressable's control, headless and headed, and the HUD's own send() for select_unit and move_unit; no user and no device pressed anything.
The headed run is local, on one macOS machine, on the local display; hosted CI runs the headless check and has not run it yet.
The criterion `autoridade` stays open: a job that survives closing the screen and bursts against the 64 tasks and 128 events a phase are not measured, and end_turn is one synchronous GDScript call.
D22 and D23 are out: nothing here recreates the application, so the HUD never reconnects to a new one.
The cycles measure nodes, orphans, bindings, subscriptions, pending work, connections and the epoch; they do not measure time, frame cost or memory, and OBJECT_COUNT is recorded, not asserted.
The previous-host control does not apply: there is no C++.
Hosted CI for test:consumer:civ-lite and the Pages publication are pending.
